answer: A handset's radio fingerprint makes a cheap Sybil farm expensive. At enrollment, three scanners record the transmitter's carrier offset, I/Q imbalance and transient ramp — a whisper-quiet signature no two radios share. Random beacons then summon each identity to transmit within seconds from its claimed lagoon-side inlet of coverage; scanners compare the live fingerprint with enrollment and reject duplicates. Forging one identity needs a separate calibrated radio, so cost rises per fake. Limits: firmware updates drift fingerprints, so re-enrollment and a bond for failed checks are required.
